_README: Synthetic statement spec for the P12 test run. Fill this in from what
HARD CONSTRAINTS, each one a real failure mode rather than a style note:
* close_date must be ON OR AFTER every test receipt's date. _buildReceiptPool
(reconcile.js:524) drops any receipt dated past stmt.end, and a dropped
receipt reads Missing receipt instead of the case you meant to test.
* cardholders[].name must EXACTLY equal Cardholders col C for that employee.
_buildCardholderIndex does an exact lookup, no fuzzy matching — the
proposal report prints the exact string each row needs.
* vendor must be the receipt's REAL merchant (Submissions col T).
bills, and both tables are permanent. A made-up vendor is a permanent
wrong pairing, not a discardable test artifact.
* ref numbers must all be distinct — statementParse flags duplicates.
* amount is what the STATEMENT says. For an exact match it equals the
receipt's col K; for the near-miss case it is deliberately higher.

charges._case: EXACT MATCH -> Matched -> Ready. Amount = row R1 col K exactly.
charges.vendor: THE HOME DEPOT #2708  GRAND RAPIDS MI

charges._case: EXACT MATCH -> Matched -> Ready. Amount = row R2 col K exactly.
NEAR MISS -> charge is OVER the receipt by 3.47, so the matcher says 'an unprinted tip?'. Drives the Override Amount -> col K transcription and its four guards. Set amount = R3 col K + 3.47.

charges._case: MISSING RECEIPT -> no test row matches this at all. This is what puts a line in the chase email to the cardholder and into Laura's full list. Vendor here is NOT learned (nothing bills), so it may be invented.

DOUBLE MATCHED -> include ONLY if two picked rows share an amount AND a cardholder (the proposal report says whether they do). One charge, two equally good receipts -> narrow Receipt Row (col H) to one, then tick Approve. Delete this charge if there is no collision.

_not_on_the_statement: Row R6 deliberately gets NO charge. It must still read Pending at the end —
that is the standing rail 'nothing bills without a matching statement charge',
and it is the one assertion that proves the gate actually holds.
